rooms.description: The great central hall of the chapel, its choir and high altar still recognisable through a thigh-deep skin of brackish water. The roof is high and shadowed; faint red rune-marks gleam on the floor below the surface. Side chapels open off east and west, and the inner chapel approach lies further north.

interactables.description: A floor flagstone in the nave is cracked through and sits unsupported over a drop into the chapel undercroft.

actionData.detectMessage: You see the cracked flagstone shimmer beneath the water — a step-thin shell over a drop. You skirt around it.
actionData.dodgeMessage: You feel the flagstone start to give and throw your weight onto the next one as it shatters into the dark water beneath.
actionData.damageMessage: A flagstone shatters beneath your foot — you fall hard against the rim of the drop, water rushing up around your ribs! (-{damage} HP)

rooms.description: A small side chapel off the nave, drier than the rest of the temple, dedicated by the carving above its lintel to the Watcher of Dawn. A bronze tide-bell hangs at the chapel's heart, salt-greened but intact, the pull-rope still sound. This is the first bell of the hymn.

interactables.label: bronze tide-bell of Dawn
interactables.description: The first bell of the Mariner's Hymn. Pull the rope.

actionData.advanceMessage: You haul on the rope. The bronze bell sings out a deep clear note that runs through the chapel stone — and somewhere far below, the chapel itself answers, almost imperceptibly. The hymn has begun.
actionData.resetMessage: The bell rings hollowly, but the chapel does not answer. The hymn has slipped — return to the start.
actionData.alreadySolvedMessage: The bell of Dawn is silent now. Its note has been given.

rooms.description: The southern side chapel, dedicated to the Watcher of Dusk by its setting-sun lintel. A second bronze tide-bell hangs at its heart. Salt-eater fungus blooms along the wet wall in a sour grey-yellow growth.

rooms.description: A long stone-vaulted corridor descending toward the chapel undercroft, its floor angling steeper as it goes. The walls hold high alcoves where the bronze tide-bells of past Wardens once tolled — most are gone, but one remains in its niche, carved in the shape of a storm-anvil. The roof creaks faintly above.

rooms.name: Crypt Chamber
rooms.description: A circular chamber at the bottom of the corridor, the floor a single round slab inscribed with a five-pointed star. A bronze star-bell hangs above it in a frame of dark iron — the fourth of the hymn's bells. A figure in salt-stained robes stands by the bell-frame, the Tide-Speaker, who tolls these bells now in ways the Wardens never sang. The air is thick, stagnant, gritty in the lungs.

rooms.description: A high-vaulted chamber beyond the crypt — the chapel's true heart, dry and warm where the rest is cold and flooded. A great bronze sea-altar of fitted scales stands in the center, its central depression empty. Above it the fifth and largest tide-bell hangs from the vault — the Sealed-Eye Bell. To the east a wall recess shows the joints of a hidden door, sealed for now.

interactables.label: Sealed-Eye Bell
interactables.description: The fifth and largest tide-bell, hanging from the vault. Pull the rope to ring out the final note of the Mariner's Hymn — and to open the way to whatever sleeps beyond.

actionData.successMessage: You pull the rope. The great Sealed-Eye Bell rings out a deep all-encompassing note that rolls up through the chapel and out to sea — the hymn is complete. With a long stone groan, the doors at the north of the sanctum swing inward, revealing the way to Korlach's lair.
actionData.resetMessage: The Sealed-Eye Bell rings hollow. The hymn has slipped — return to the bell of Dawn and begin again.
actionData.alreadySolvedMessage: The Sealed-Eye Bell hangs silent now. The way ahead is open.

interactables.label: bronze sea-altar of fitted scales
interactables.description: The altar's central depression is the exact size of a Mariner's Conch — placing one would, by the chapel's old rite, open the seaward vault.

actionData.promptText: The sea-altar's central depression waits. Which item from your pack do you place here?
actionData.successMessage: You set the Mariner's Conch into the depression. It seats with a soft hollow boom that runs through the bronze of the altar and into the floor — and the joints of the eastern wall ease open with a long sigh of trapped air, revealing the seaward vault beyond.
actionData.failureMessage: Nothing happens. Whatever you tried to place, the sea-altar does not recognise it.

interactables.label: softly glowing red wall-runes
interactables.description: Carved runes in the sanctum walls, charged with a slow arcane curse that hooks at the willpower of whoever stands beneath them.

actionData.detectMessage: You see the runes set into the sanctum walls glowing faintly red — a slow curse hooked to whoever stands beneath them. You set your jaw before you cross.
actionData.dodgeMessage: You hold your mind firm as you cross, the curse breaking against the wall of your will.
actionData.damageMessage: The runes flare red as you cross — a hooked cold thought drives in behind your eyes! (-{damage} HP)

rooms.name: Mariner's Vault
rooms.description: A small dry chamber behind the sea-altar, shelved in dark stone. The shelves hold the votive offerings of mariners across centuries — small bronze tokens, sealed clay jars, scrimshaw, and at the back, a stone-lidded reliquary bearing the marks of older Wardens than even Old Wren has tales of.

rooms.name: Korlach's Lair
rooms.description: The deepest chamber of the chapel — a vast oval flooded waist-deep in dark salt water, the centre dominated by a great bronze ring sunk into the floor like a mooring-stone for whatever lives down here. The reliquary on the back wall threatens to fall the instant your weight crosses the threshold.
